name: Fender AB763 Twin Reverb (vibrato channel, complete)
description: 1965 blackface Twin Reverb, vibrato channel from input jack to speakers: V2A, the AB763 treble/middle/bass stack, volume with the 120 pF bright switch, V2B (sharing its 820 Ohm cathode with the idle normal-channel V1B, whose mixer also loads the phase inverter input), the 12AT7 reverb driver, reverb transformer and 4AB3C1B tank, V4A recovery and reverb pot, the 3.3 MOhm/470 kOhm dry/wet mix into V4B, the neon/LDR tremolo with its 12AX7 phase-shift oscillator and driver, the 12AT7 long-tail phase inverter with 820/47 Ohm feedback, 4 x 6L6GC (matched pairs), the 125A29A output transformer and 2 x 12-inch 8 Ohm speakers, powered by the real 340-0-340 VAC silicon supply with its choke and B+ chain (sag, ripple and the tremolo's supply interaction emerge from the circuit). Signal cuts (one-sample current coupling) sit only where the downstream load is tiny against the node's own conductance: after the V2B, V1B and V4B coupling caps. The NFB loop (phase inverter + power stage) stays in one solve.

sources.title: Fender 'Twin Reverb-Amp AB763' factory schematic: vibrato oscillator and roach driver (V5B grid on the junction of the two 0.01 uF caps and the 1 MOhm leg, returned through 1 MOhm to the pedal jack and 2.2 MOhm to the -52 V bias; 3M-RA speed + 100 kOhm on the 0.02 uF node; 50K-RA intensity; V5B 100 kOhm / 25 uF cathode, +17 V; neon + 100 kOhm and 10 MOhm on the plate, +380 V)

Rob Robinette, AB763 Twin Reverb layout (DIYLC) v2.18: part values, B+ node voltages (460/458/450/410 V), -52 V bias, 125P34A 340-0-340 VAC, 125A29A 2k:4 OT, 125A20B reverb transformer, 125C1A 4 H choke
Rob Robinette, How the AB763 Deluxe Reverb Works (shared AB763 circuit description: reverb mix, tremolo roach, LTP)
Rob Robinette, AB763 model differences (Twin: 47 Ohm NFB tail, .047 uF mid cap, .001 uF PI coupling, solid-state rectifier)
D. T. Yeh, J. O. Smith, Discretization of the '59 Fender Bassman tone stack, DAFx 2006 (TMB topology)

Fender Electric Instrument Co., 'Deluxe Reverb-Amp AB763' schematic (factory drawing with voltage chart: 420/415 V power stage, +325 V PI, -35 V grids, 12AT7 reverb driver +410 V / +8.7 V, V5A +270 V / +2.1 V, V5B +345 V / +17 V, PI +170/+180 V plates, +77 V cathodes; transformer list TR1 125P23B, TR2 125C3A, TR3 125A1A, TR4 125A20B) [AB763 circuit shared with the Twin Reverb: vibrato oscillator / roach driver and phase-inverter feedback wiring]

Rob Robinette, AB763 reverb circuit and tremolo circuit diagrams (reverb pedal 'open = on' on the recovery grid; vibrato pedal 'closed = on'; 2.2 MOhm jump start to -55 V) [AB763 circuit shared with the Twin Reverb: vibrato oscillator / roach driver and phase-inverter feedback wiring]

Music Electronics Forum, 'Fender AB763 style optocoupled tremolo circuit question' (V5B 100 kOhm cathode resistor; 10 MOhm keeps the neon able to extinguish) [AB763 circuit shared with the Twin Reverb: vibrato oscillator / roach driver and phase-inverter feedback wiring]

io.note: outputVoltsPerFS calibrated so the clean Twin sits at the legacy model's loudness (speaker volts; ~40 V peak when dimed = about -6 dBFS). outputVoltsPerFS 80 -> 61.672 (2026-11-10): keeps the shipped level within 1 dB of the previous release after the refitted valve cards (DI level -2.26 dB at the same scale). 61.672 -> 76.131 (2026-11-10): the roach-driver fix (V5B grid on om, not ot) took the idle lamp glow (light ~0.04) off the LDR, which had been shunting the vibrato channel with vibrato off; DI level +1.83 dB at the same scale (3 s riff, 0.5 V peak, unit defaults)

controls.label: Reverb footswitch
controls.note: Reverb footswitch: 0 = open (reverb on, as with no pedal plugged in), 1 = closed (shorts the tank return at the V4A grid). Legacy RvOn maps inverted

controls.label: Speed
controls.note: 3 MOhm reverse-audio rheostat in series with 100 kOhm in the first shunt leg of the phase-shift ladder; clockwise = faster

controls.label: Intensity
controls.note: 50 kOhm reverse-audio pot from the vibrato mixing node to ground; the roach LDR shunts its wiper to ground

controls.label: Vibrato on
controls.note: Vibrato footswitch (closed = on): grounds the oscillator grid return so it oscillates. Open (default, as with no pedal plugged in), the oscillator is cut off

controls.label: Variac
controls.note: Variac: scales the mains (every transformer secondary, including the bias winding) from 75 % at 0 through nominal at 0.5 to 108 % at 1 (90 / 120 / 130 VAC on a 120 V amp)
controls.modNote: Not on the original amplifier: a variac on the mains, as players did to run the amp at lower line voltage. Offered as a mod; at full scale the amp sees its rated mains.

parts.label: V5B tremolo (neon) driver
parts.note: Grid on the ladder's middle node om (the junction of the two 0.01 uF caps and the 1 MOhm leg), DC return through that 1 MOhm to the footswitch node oj, as drawn on the Fender Twin Reverb AB763 and Deluxe Reverb AB763 schematics. Footswitch open, oj sits at the bias supply through 2.2 MOhm, so the driver is cut off with the oscillator and the lamp is dark. (Fixed 2026-11-10: the grid was on ot, the 0.02 uF / speed-rheostat node, whose DC return is ground: the driver idled lit, and B+2 ripple through the 0.02 uF cap swung the lamp 0-0.8 with the playing signal while the vibrato was off.)

parts.note: unverified: DCR, leakage, primary inductance (20 H plate-to-plate) and saturation flux are typical values for an 85 W OT; secondary phased so the 820 Ohm tail feedback is negative (checked: 200 Hz gain drops 3.7 dB with the feedback resistor in, the other phasing oscillates). Winding capacitance: CWA/CWB with their loss resistors

parts.label: OT half-primary capacitance (A)
parts.note: unverified: half-primary self-capacitance with its loss (dielectric, copper and eddy losses at the leakage resonance) as a lumped 470 pF + 2.2 kOhm from each plate to the centre tap. A lossless lumped capacitance rings with the leakage inductance (~95 kHz) and the tail feedback turns that into an oscillation; with no capacitance at all, a tube cutting off throws sub-microsecond kilovolt flyback spikes. With the loss term the engine and ngspice agree within 0.2 % at heavy drive
